background_notes.fact: A bounded multilinear map between normed spaces is continuous; diagonal evaluation gives a continuous homogeneous polynomial. Finite sums and compositions of continuous multilinear constructions give continuous polynomial maps. On the Fourier Sobolev spaces here, P and P0 are bounded projections, Dinv and Dinv2 are bounded on each H^s, H1 embeds continuously in L2, and Dinv:L2->H1 is bounded also without a mean-zero restriction, by annihilation of the constant mode.

grounds.reason: Provides the inverse-derivative L2-to-H1 estimate, the H1 algebra estimate and unitarity of S_t.
Supplies the weighted Fourier norms and L2=H0.
P0 selects the zero coefficient.
P removes that coefficient.
Inverse derivatives have bounded multipliers for nonzero integer frequencies and vanish at zero.
For fixed positive tau each term is a finite composition with finite scalar coefficients.

background_notes.justification: For a bounded m-linear map, telescope the difference between its values on two tuples, changing one entry at a time; its norm is bounded by a finite sum of products with one difference factor. This proves continuity and the diagonal polynomial assertion. The projection and multiplier bounds follow termwise from the weighted square sums, using |k|>=1 when k!=0. Apply N006 to P f to extend Dinv's estimate to arbitrary L2 inputs. These facts justify each quadratic/cubic construction in S001.

background_notes.fact: On the normalized torus, (f,g)->P0(fg) is a continuous complex-bilinear scalar form on L2 x L2 with |P0(fg)|<=||f||2||g||2. In particular f->P0(f^2) is a continuous quadratic polynomial, with |P0(f^2)|<=||f||2^2; this does not assume f is real.

background_notes.justification: For polynomials P0(fg)=sum_k hat f(k)hat g(-k); Cauchy-Schwarz for the two square-summable coefficient sequences gives the bound. The form extends by polynomial density; equivalently the product is integrable by the integral Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. The difference identity f^2-g^2=(f-g)f+g(f-g) gives continuity on the diagonal.

background_notes.fact: The operators S_t, P, P0, Dinv, spatial differentiation and spatial multiplication preserve smooth periodic functions; S_t depends smoothly on time on such inputs. The D013 Fourier formula is well defined and smooth on smooth inputs, agrees with its polynomial formula, has zero mean, and preserves reality when all inputs are real. Consequently all smooth-path operations in S001-S003 are legitimate.

The Airy multiplier is exp(i*t*k^3).

background_notes.justification: Repeated integration by parts gives arbitrarily fast Fourier decay for a smooth periodic function. Multiplication of its coefficients by any fixed polynomial preserves such decay, which justifies time and space differentiation of S_t termwise, uniformly on compact time intervals. Products preserve smoothness by the product rule. For R2, |eta|<=2 and 1/|k|<=1 on its nonzero modes. For any nonnegative integer m, 1+|a+b+c| <= (1+|a|)(1+|b|)(1+|c|), so the weighted absolute sum of output coefficients is at most (tau/9) times the product of the three weighted absolute input sums. These are finite by smoothness. Hence the series and all spatial derivatives converge absolutely and Fourier truncations give the same smooth extension. Under simultaneous frequency reversal, alpha,beta,Phi change sign, eta is conjugated and the 1/(ik) prefactor is conjugated as well. Thus real inputs give conjugate symmetry. All other listed operators also preserve conjugate symmetry and the asserted zero modes.

background_notes.fact: For a jointly smooth periodic integrand G(s,x) on a compact time interval, the primitive integral_a^t G(s,x) ds is smooth in space and differentiable in time with derivative G(t,x); the same holds in every finite Sobolev norm. Finitely many continuous interval paths with matching endpoint values concatenate continuously. A residual assembled from continuous increments rho_n with rho_n(t_n)=0 is continuous and has derivative rho_n' on each open step, hence almost everywhere.

background_notes.justification: On compact time-space sets all derivatives of a smooth integrand are bounded, so differentiation under the spatial integral is justified by uniform convergence of difference quotients, and the time derivative of the primitive follows from the difference quotient of an integral of a continuous function. Applying this to F_n,C_n,Q_n and rho_n gives S003's derivatives. Finite endpoint matching proves continuity by the one-sided limits. The exceptional set of finitely many grid points has measure zero, giving the asserted a.e. identity.
